implementation_statement: Enterprise access control policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.3 (P06) apply to the PDPP. Procedures PRC-02.1 to PRC-02.4 cover provisioning, external user lifecycle, privileged access, and break-glass access.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: Workforce accounts in SYS-01, the ERP, and the payment hub are provisioned by identity governance from HR events and role templates approved by the system owner. External users in SYS-01 (about 41,000 subcontractor, design-team, and owner users) are invited by project teams and must be removed at project closeout. Gap: 1,140 external accounts on projects closed more than 90 days were still active at assessment, and AQ-1 users still reach SYS-01 with local accounts outside identity governance (POAM-001).
evidence: Identity governance role templates; SYS-01 external user report; P07 AC-2 results

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Joiner, mover, and leaver events flow automatically from the HR system to identity governance, which provisions and removes PDPP roles through SSO connectors.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: Workforce accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled automatically by identity governance. SYS-01 cannot disable external users automatically, so project teams run a monthly report; the report was not worked on 9 of 25 sampled projects (POAM-001).
evidence: Inactivity job logs; SYS-01 external inactivity report

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Account creation, modification, disabling, and removal in identity governance and the ERP generate audit records forwarded to the SIEM, with alerts on changes to payment roles.
evidence: SIEM use case list; identity governance audit log

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Sessions to the ERP and payment hub time out after 15 minutes of inactivity; SYS-01 web sessions after 30 minutes; users are logged out at the end of the session.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: Role-based access in SYS-01 limits each user to assigned projects; ERP roles separate project accounting, billing, AP entry, vendor master maintenance, and payment release. SSO enforces access to all PDPP applications.
evidence: SYS-01 project permission matrix; ERP role catalog

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Landing zone network policies allow only defined flows between the ERP, integration platform, payment hub, and bank gateways; the file transfer gateway accepts bank connections only from allow-listed bank addresses.
evidence: Network policy export; gateway allow list

implementation_statement: Role design separates vendor master maintenance (Payment Operations), invoice entry (AP), and payment release (Treasury), with dual approval for all wires and ACH batches above $250,000. Gap: 4 enterprise users kept emergency vendor-master rights after a 2026-03 system cutover, and AQ-1 AP staff can create payees and release payments in the AQ-1 ERP, whose files the payment hub accepts (POAM-002; POAM-003).
evidence: ERP segregation of duties conflict report; payment hub approval matrix

implementation_statement: Least privilege is enforced by role templates; administrator rights in the ERP and payment hub are granted only through PAM for approved windows.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Security functions (role administration, payment hub approval matrix changes, SSO configuration) are restricted to named administrators in PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged accounts, vaulted in PAM, for administrative work; daily work uses standard accounts.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Privileged accounts for the PDPP are limited to 38 named ERP, integration, and gateway administrators, reviewed quarterly.
PAM records and the SIEM log every privileged session and every use of payment hub and ERP administrative functions.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: SSO locks an account for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts and applies risk-based blocking; SYS-01 external users authenticate through the vendor's identity service with lockout after 5 failures.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: The SSO sign-in page displays the system use notification approved by Legal; SYS-01 shows the same notice to external users at sign-in.
Managed laptops and desktops lock after 15 minutes; managed tablets and phones after 5 minutes.
The ERP and payment hub terminate sessions after 12 hours absolute or 15 minutes idle; bank gateway sessions close at the end of each transfer.
Remote access to PDPP administration is only through the zero-trust access service with device checks and MFA; there is no direct internet access to ERP or gateway servers.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: All remote sessions are encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher through the zero-trust access service.
Office and trailer Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication with certificates for managed devices; guest Wi-Fi is isolated from company networks.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: External systems that exchange data with the PDPP (owner portals, federal invoicing portals, subcontractor systems, e-signature service) are listed with approved data types. Personal email for FCI or pay app data is prohibited (POL-05 4.6).
Project photos and descriptions for public posting are reviewed by two named approvers in Corporate Communications; federal project content also needs Federal Group approval.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Training standard STD-05.1 under POL-05 sets awareness and role-based training for all workforce.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Annual awareness training and monthly phishing simulations for all workforce; the 2026 click rate was 3.1% and the report rate 64%.
evidence: Learning system completion report; phishing metrics

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Training covers insider threat indicators, including fictitious vendors and unusual payment requests.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Role-based payment fraud training is required for project managers, project accountants, AP, Payment Operations, and Treasury. Gap: 81% completion among project managers, and AQ-1 AP staff have not been trained (POAM-011).
Audit logging standard STD-01.4 under POL-01 applies to the PDPP.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: Logged events include sign-ins, role changes, vendor master and bank-account changes, payment approvals and releases, and gateway file transfers. Gap: bulk drawing downloads and permission changes in SYS-01 are kept by the vendor for 90 days and are not forwarded to the SIEM (POAM-018).
evidence: Event list in STD-01.4; SIEM source list

implementation_statement: Records include time, user, source, event type, object, and outcome in a normalized SIEM schema.
Vendor master change records add old and new bank values (masked), the requester, the call-back reference, and the approver.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: The SIEM alerts when a PDPP log source stops sending for 60 minutes.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews PDPP alerts 24x7, including new inbox rules, risky sign-ins, and payment-role anomalies in the enterprise tenant. Gap: the AQ-1 email tenant and AQ-1 ERP send no logs to the SIEM (POAM-004).
evidence: SOC review records; SIEM source list

implementation_statement: SIEM correlation and SOAR playbooks link identity, email, ERP, and payment hub events.
SIEM correlates mailbox events with vendor master changes, for example a bank-change request that follows a new inbox rule on the requester's mailbox.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Logs are written to a separate log archive account with write-once retention; PDPP administrators cannot delete them.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Logs are kept 1 year online and 7 years in the archive to meet SOX and the 6-year CMMC artifact rule.
Logging agents and API collectors are deployed by the platform for all PDPP components except SYS-01 download events (see AU-2).
Assessment and authorization standard STD-01.2 sets annual independent assessment of tier-1 systems.
Internal Audit assessed 44 PDPP controls from 2026-07-13 to 2026-08-28 (P07). The enterprise FCI scope self-assessment for CMMC Level 1 was completed 2026-01-30.
evidence: P07 assessment plan and results; Level 1 self-assessment

implementation_statement: Assessors are Internal Audit staff who do not design or operate PDPP controls; CMMC specialists are co-sourced.
Bank connectivity agreements with the three treasury banks define file formats, encryption, keys, and contacts; interface agreements cover SYS-01 to ERP and ERP to payroll.
PDPP weaknesses are tracked in the enterprise POA&M in the GRC platform (P07 poam.csv) and reviewed monthly.
The COO is the authorizing official equivalent and approved continued operation with conditions on 2026-09-14 (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring metrics (payment exceptions, access certification, SIEM coverage, vulnerability SLAs) are reported monthly to the CISO and quarterly to the risk committee.
Configuration and change management standard STD-01.5 and procedure PRC-01.3 apply.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: ERP servers, integration platform, and gateway appliances are built from hardened images defined as code; SYS-01 tenant settings are documented in a configuration baseline reviewed quarterly.

control_name: Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency
provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Posture management compares running configuration with baselines daily and opens tickets for drift.

Changes go through the change advisory board with risk rating, testing, and approval; payment file mappings and bank connection settings are high-risk changes needing Treasury approval. Gap: 3 of 40 sampled integration changes were emergency changes not approved afterward (POAM-005).

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: Changes are tested in a non-production environment with test bank files before release.
Security impact analysis is required for changes to payment roles, bank connections, and SYS-01 sharing settings.
Only release engineers can deploy to production, through the pipeline and PAM.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Configuration settings follow the enterprise hardening standard; SYS-01 sharing defaults are set to project members only, with public links disabled.
Gateway and ERP servers run only required services and ports; unused ERP modules are disabled.

The CMDB lists PDPP servers, appliances, and integrations. Endpoints that reach SYS-01 are inventoried in device management. Gap: about 18% of rugged jobsite tablets (about 580) are not enrolled (POAM-013).
Inventory updates automatically when devices enroll or servers are built.
Users cannot install software on managed laptops; tablets install only from the managed app catalog.
Contingency and disaster recovery standard STD-03.3 under POL-03 applies.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: PDPP contingency plan v3 sets RTO and RPO from the BIA (P05 BP-01 to BP-05), names alternate procedures, and lists recovery roles.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: Critical assets are the ERP database, vendor master, payment hub, bank gateway, and the SYS-01 nightly export.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: Recovery team members complete annual contingency training.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: The ERP and payment hub were tested in the 2026-05-09 tier-1 DR test. Gap: the SYS-01 export has never been restored into a usable read-only copy (POAM-008).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Backups are copied to a separate backup account in a second region and weekly to COLO-2.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: A warm standby of the ERP and payment hub runs in a second region of Cloud provider A.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: ERP database backups run every 15 minutes (logs) and nightly (full) to immutable storage; SYS-01 data is exported nightly to company storage.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: ERP recovery met its 24-hour RTO in the 2026-05-09 test (19 hours). Gap: SYS-01 depends on the vendor's 24-hour contract RTO against the BIA RTO of 8 hours for field execution (POAM-008).
Identification and authentication standard STD-02.2 applies.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: All workforce users authenticate through SSO with unique identifiers; external SYS-01 users have unique vendor accounts with MFA enforced by the vendor.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Privileged accounts use phishing-resistant FIDO2 security keys through PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: All non-privileged users use MFA. Treasury, Payment Operations, AP, and executives use FIDO2 security keys; the 2,900 project management staff still use number-matching push, which an adversary-in-the-middle phishing page can relay (POAM-017).

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Authentication uses replay-resistant protocols (modern federation with signed, time-limited assertions).
Device certificates identify managed devices; conditional access requires a compliant device for ERP and payment hub access.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Identifiers come from HR employee numbers and are never reused.

Passwords follow STD-02.2 (14 characters minimum, breached-password check); service account secrets are vaulted and rotated. Gap: the payment file transfer gateway management console still had the vendor default password (P07 new finding, changed 2026-08-13; POAM-007).
evidence: PAM vault report; P07 IA-5 result

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Password policy enforces length, breached-password screening, and no forced periodic change except on suspicion.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: External users (subcontractors, designers, owners) are identified by vendor accounts tied to their company email; MFA is enforced for all external SYS-01 users.
New payees are identity-proofed before activation: tax ID match, business registration lookup, and bank account ownership verification through the validation service.
regulatory_driver: FAR 52.232-33(b) (EFT accuracy for the company's own SAM record)

implementation_statement: Incident response and resilience policy POL-03 applies.
SOC staff, Payment Operations, and Treasury complete annual incident response training, including the BEC runbook (P08).
The BEC runbook was tested in a technical tabletop on 2026-02-24; the disclosure committee did not take part (see IR-8).
Incidents are handled by the SOC under the P08 runbooks. Gap: the AQ-1 payment fraud event (EV-2026-04) was handled by AQ-1 finance for 6 days before reaching the SOC (POAM-010).
Incidents are tracked in SOC case management with severity, timeline, and closure.

Incidents are reported to the SOC within 1 hour (POL-03 4.2); external reporting follows the P08 notification matrix, including DFARS 252.204-7012(c) if CUI is involved (the SYS-01 CUI finding makes this possible, P03).
Incident response plan v5 with runbooks and the materiality procedure PRC-03.2. Gap: no payment fraud scenario in the materiality playbook and no guidance on related occurrences (POAM-009).
Maintenance standard STD-01.6 applies.
ERP vendor support connects only through PAM with approval and session recording.
Media protection standard STD-04.2 applies.
Endpoints and server media are wiped with NIST SP 800-88 methods or destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-07 Facilities and physical security; colocation
responsible_role: Vice President, Corporate Facilities and Security
implementation_statement: Physical security standard STD-01.7 applies.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-07 Facilities and physical security; colocation
responsible_role: Vice President, Corporate Facilities and Security
implementation_statement: Colocation and office access is badge-controlled and logged; Cloud provider A physical controls are covered by its SOC 2 report.
Planning policy and this SSP follow STD-01.2.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: This SSP (version 2.0) describes the PDPP boundary, controls, and inheritance; reviewed annually.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Workforce acknowledge POL-05 at hire and annually; external SYS-01 users accept the terms of use at first sign-in.
The enterprise uses the SP 800-53B Moderate baseline for tier-1 systems, tailored per SSP.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Personnel security procedures sit under POL-01 and POL-02.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Background checks are completed before access for Treasury, Payment Operations, AP, and administrator roles.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Access is disabled the same business day as termination. Gap: 3 of 60 sampled terminations were late (2 AQ-1 staff by 4 and 7 days; 1 field engineer by 2 days) (POAM-014).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Sanctions follow PRC-01.1 and are documented.
Risk assessment standard STD-01.1 applies.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: The PDPP is categorized Moderate (section 6) with payment integrity supplements.
The 2026 enterprise risk analysis (P01) covers PDPP risks, including payment fraud and CUI exposure.
Supply chain risks for PDPP vendors (platform, ERP, banks, validation and e-signature services) are assessed in the vendor program.
Weekly authenticated scans of PDPP servers and appliances; remediation SLAs 15 days critical, 30 days high. Gap: 4 of 60 sampled findings on the integration platform were past SLA (POAM-015).
Risk responses are recorded in P01 and the POA&M.

responsible_role: Vice President, Project Controls and Systems
implementation_statement: Critical components identified: vendor master, payment approval workflow, bank gateway, SYS-01 drawing repository.
Contracts for PDPP vendors include security, notification, and data return terms; federal flowdown terms apply where FCI is handled.
Design principles: least privilege for payment roles, defense in depth for bank connectivity, no single person can complete a payment.

External services are tiered and assessed; the project management platform vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report is reviewed annually. Gap: no current SOC report review for the e-signature and bank account validation services (POAM-012).
Custom integration code is peer reviewed and scanned in the pipeline before release.
No unsupported components remain in the PDPP; the AQ-1 ERP (outside the boundary) runs a supported version until migration.
System and communications protection standards STD-04.1 and STD-01.5 apply.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Internet-facing endpoints (file-transfer portal, Capital Program Portal) sit behind the landing zone DDoS protection and web application firewall.
PDPP components sit in a dedicated workload account with deny-by-default policies; the bank gateway is in its own subnet. Gap: three AQ-1 VPN subnets can reach the integration platform (POAM-016).
evidence: Network policy export; P07 SC-7 test

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Network policies deny by default and allow by exception.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: All PDPP traffic uses TLS 1.2 or higher or SFTP. Gap: payment files to bank 3 are encrypted in transit but not signed or hash-checked end to end (POAM-006).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Cryptographic protection in transit uses FIPS-validated modules provided by the cloud platform and gateway.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Keys are managed in the cloud key management service with customer-managed keys for the ERP database and backups; bank file keys are rotated yearly.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Approved cryptography per STD-04.1.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Session tokens are bound to compliant devices for ERP and payment hub access; token theft from an unmanaged device is rejected.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: ERP database, backups, and gateway storage are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys; SYS-01 encrypts at rest per its SOC 2 report.
System and information integrity procedures sit under POL-01 and POL-04.
Patches are applied within the STD-01.5 timelines; ERP patches follow the monthly release cycle.
EDR on all PDPP servers and managed endpoints; email attachment and link scanning in the productivity suite.

24x7 SOC monitoring with BEC use cases (new inbox rules, impossible travel, adversary-in-the-middle token use, vendor master change after mailbox anomaly). Gap: no monitoring of the AQ-1 email tenant (POAM-004).
System-generated alerts for payment-role anomalies page the SOC on duty.
Threat intelligence on payment fraud campaigns and lookalike domains is received and acted on; lookalike domain monitoring covers all company brands.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Integrity of payment data is protected by role separation, approval workflow, and positive pay. Gap: end-to-end file integrity checking is missing for bank 3 (POAM-006).
The payment hub hashes each approved file and the gateway verifies the hash before sending to banks 1 and 2; bank 3 does not support signed files yet (POAM-006).
Integrity check failures raise SOC incidents automatically.

Bank details are validated against the validation service and by call-back before release. Gap: payment files from the AQ-1 ERP are accepted without enterprise payee verification, and 4 of 60 sampled enterprise bank changes lacked a recorded call-back (POAM-003).
Records are retained per the records schedule, including 7 years for financial records and 6 years for security documentation.
Supply chain risk management standard STD-01.3 applies.
Supply chain controls include Section 889 screening of IT and network equipment purchased for the PDPP.
Acquisition strategy uses authorized resellers and the approved manufacturer list.
Tier-1 PDPP suppliers are reviewed annually.
Planned: payment release and vendor master changes allowed only from compliant managed devices during staffed hours, with exceptions approved by Treasury.
Behavior analytics flag atypical use of payment-role and project manager accounts (new countries, mass mailbox searches for "remittance" or "ACH"). Gap: not available for AQ-1 accounts (POAM-004).

Vendor master changes, payment approvals, and releases are bound to named users authenticated with security keys. Gap: call-back evidence is free text rather than a structured, attributable record (POAM-003).

control_name: Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes
implementation_statement: Planned: the pipeline will block deployment of payment file mapping changes without a linked approved change and Treasury approval.

implementation_statement: Vendor master, payment history, and approval logs are copied daily to a separate backup account with write-once retention.
